GLOBAL-DQ-038.reason: The same asymmetry as GLOBAL-DQ-037: it asserts that every medal-round event carries the medal_related property, and Golf's medal rounds are 5020 stroke-play events of which 6 award a medal. Reports 4764 of 4768.

GLOBAL-DQ-007.reason: 10482 of 20547 people reached through the sport hold no date of birth. Half a registry is a completeness proportion rather than a repair list, and the sport's registry is large and old; the rows are correct and there are simply a great many of them.

GLOBAL-DQ-071.reason: 159 of the 170 events reported are NO_PARTICIPANTS_NOT_FINISHED_EVENT, and they are the sport's calendar running ahead of its entry lists: Hero World Challenge is dated December 2026 and Andalucia Open de Espana November 2026, announced and not yet fielded. The 11 NO_PARTICIPANTS_FINISHED_EVENT rows are the ones worth reading and stay visible under the same check - all eleven are match-play events from 2004 to 2010, WGC Accenture Match Play and HSBC World Match Play among them, and not one of them left with the client boundary. GLOBAL-DQ-064.reason: eligible_count is 0 and this is a sentinel: the template's eligible population is the statistic that uses the 1429 Team field at all, and Golf writes no row into it. The scope is correct and the population is legitimately empty.

Match play alone would satisfy the prerequisite; the sport does not.

_names.STATISTIC_TYPE_ID: 11 Competition Stats, called Comp.Rank in this project. Declared for the reach paths of GLOBAL-DQ-007 and GLOBAL-DQ-009 only, not because the sport's Comp.Rank layer has been read - it has not. The layer is not empty: 841 tournament-owned records holding 7179 people, measured 2026-08-20
_names.STATISTIC_OWNER_TYPE_ID: 3 tournament, by decision of 2026-08-20. The sport writes Comp.Rank at two owner levels and both are real - 841 tournament-owned and 200 tournament_stage-owned, measured that day, all of them statistic type 11. Only the tournament level is in the client's scope, so the stage-owned 200 are out of client scope rather than absent, and a check that returns nothing for them is not reporting clean data. Recorded here so the run stops choosing the busier of the two for itself, which is a count and not a documented fact
_names.SHARD_ID: 11 statistic_participants11 and statistic_data11. No person in the sport is reachable through that shard alone - all 7179 are also event participants, lineup members or sport registrants, measured 2026-08-20 - so the branch changes neither check's population today, and will once the layer is regenerated

_names.RESULT_MEDAL_TYPE_ID: 501 Medal, holding gold, silver and bronze only

Six names are each carried by two ids, so the list cannot be rebuilt from names. round_typeFK 0 is deliberately absent: it resolves to no round_type row and is the missing-round-type gap rather than a round the sport holds

_names.NOT_STARTED_DESC_LIST: 1 Not started, the only not-started status description the sport uses
_names.MEDAL_ROUND_TYPE_LIST: 9 Final and 173 Final, the only two rounds carrying a 501 Medal result; measured 2026-08-20 over 11383 medalled events, and every other round returned zero. 323 Finals Summary awards none despite its name
_names.FINAL_ROUND_TYPE_LIST: 9 Final and 173 Final, the same two: this sport awards its whole medal set inside the one Final rather than deciding bronze in its own match
_names.RANK_MAX_PLAUSIBLE: 200, chosen 2026-08-20 with the largest legitimate field at 133 participants and the highest stored rank at 127; nothing in the sport reaches 150
_names.TIMED_DISCIPLINE_LIST: all 45 disciplines the sport contests, in both its live vocabularies - the spelled-out 38-58 and the abbreviated 348-374 plus 468, 479, 557 and 642. Swimming judges nothing: every discipline is resolved on the clock, so none is left out
_names.FULL_TIME_TOLERANCE_SECONDS: 0.01, matching the precision the sport actually swims to. 557 Full-time duration is written with three decimal places throughout, and the repository's usual 1 second would be wider than most winning margins
_names.PRECISION_RESULT_TYPE_LIST: 101 Duration and 557 Full-time duration. 557 is uniformly three decimal places; 101 is not, holding 3, 2, 1, 0 and 4 places at once, which is what the check is here to report
_names.CLOCK_RESULT_TYPE_LIST: 101 Duration and 557 Full-time duration, the two fields the sport writes in clock notation. The same two ids as PRECISION_RESULT_TYPE_LIST and not the same statement: that one names the fields whose decimal scale is fixed by convention, and a sport can write a score to a fixed scale without any colon in it. GLOBAL-DQ-128 reads only values that actually carry a colon, so a field listed here that never uses one is silent rather than wrong. Measured 2026-08-21, the sport holds one value whose seconds component passes 59 - 4:99.02 - and Cycling holds 79 in 3 events on the same two ids
_names.RESULT_TIE_VALUE_TYPE_LIST: 557 Full-time duration and 101 Duration, the two quantities a place is settled from. 101 reaches 442950 of 444109 ranked participations and 557 reaches 414814, so naming both leaves almost no place unaccounted for
_names.RESULT_COMMENT_VALUE_LIST: the normalized vocabulary agreed 2026-08-20: 91 forms of the 130 the sport currently stores. It holds the canonical spelling of each marker and the compound comments as written, and deliberately excludes the duplicate spellings - DSQ, DSQ*, DISQ and DQ beside Disq.; dns. and dns dec. beside DNS; N.C. and Nc. beside NC - the unexplained ? and R?, the leaked #NAME?, and the eight forms whose own text contains a comma, which a comma-separated parameter cannot carry. Those exclusions are the point: the check reports them so the notation can be settled
_names.RESULT_COMMENT_NO_RESULT_LIST: DNS, DNF, Disq., WD, NC, Retired and OTL. R was measured out of this list on 2026-08-20: 3464 of its 3492 participations carry both a rank and a real swim time, so whatever R marks in this sport, it is not the absence of a result. The list is a subset of the value list because TOOLS/Test-Package.ps1 requires that; the rejected variant spellings are caught by the value list instead
_names.DUPLICATE_KEY_INCLUDES_EVENT_NAME: 1: this sport names an event after its discipline and distance, never after the competitors, so the name carries real information about which event it is
_names.DUPLICATE_KEY_USES_CALENDAR_DAY: 0: the sport runs the same field several times a day. Measured 2026-08-20, one stage holds up to 20 identically named events on a single day, so a calendar-day key would report the entire heat structure as duplicates
_names.PLACEHOLDER_COUNTRY_LIST: International, Unknown and Undefined. Only International occurs, on 166 stages, and GLOBAL-DQ-034 already excludes it from the test on the stage's own country; the other two are named so they are caught if they ever arrive
_names.SERIES_MIN_YEARS: 3, the repository's usual threshold for a series long enough that a break in it means something
_names.SERIES_SKIP_YEARS: 2020, the year the sport is known not to have run. It holds 96 events against roughly 2400 in each neighbouring year, so without naming it every annual series reports a break it did not have
_names.ELIMINATION_ROUND_NAME_LIST: the rounds a swimmer can go out of: heats and their three subdivisions - heats summary, fastest heats, slowest heats - plus semi finals, quarter finals, 1/8, swim-off and preliminary. The heats summary is listed deliberately: it is the aggregated ranking across all heats and is where qualification is actually decided, which the Q, R and ? markers sitting on it confirm
_names.GROUP_ROUND_NAME_LIST: the rounds nobody leaves: final, finals summary and after heats. A final is terminal, so no entry goes out of it, and the other two are aggregate views rather than swum rounds. The four round types named with a bare number - 1, 3, 10 and 11 - are in neither list on purpose: the template leaves an unjudged name silent rather than assuming it
_names.STALE_NOT_STARTED_DAYS: 2, the value GLOBAL_DQ/README.md fixes for every sport by the decision of 2026-08-06. It measures how long a not-started status went unmaintained after the event's own date, which is a property of the feed rather than of the sport, so it is not a per-sport judgement

_notApplicable.SCOPE_TYPE_ID: the sport writes its split-time layer only on distance and open-water events - 125 containers against 45602 finished events - and GLOBAL-DQ-107 asserts a container on every finished event, with SCOPE_TYPE_ID as its only parameter and no way to name the disciplines that legitimately carry one. Declaring a value here would report the sport's normal state 45477 times.

GLOBAL-DQ-146.reason: the drill-down of GLOBAL-DQ-132 and it carries that check's verdict unchanged: part of what it returns is correct by construction and will never be corrected, so the count is expected to stay above zero. A competitor entered under a neutral or refugee organization is entered under a country that is not their own on purpose. What the detail adds is that the exceptions can now be told apart from the rest one row at a time. Measured 2026-08-28 on Swimming, the sport with the largest population: 306 findings of 394 eligible participations, and every one of the 306 sits under an organization whose country is International - Russian Swimming Federation, Neutral Athletes A and B, Individual Neutral Athletes, Russian Olympic Committee. Eight of them are worth a look on their own and were invisible in the summary, where they were one number with the other 298: five participations of French competitors under Russian Olympic Committee and three under Russian Swimming Federation.

GLOBAL-DQ-132.reason: some of what it returns is correct by construction and will never be corrected, so the count is expected to stay above zero however much is repaired. Measured 2026-08-21 on Artistic Gymnastics, one of its two findings is a Russian gymnast entered under Individual Neutral Athletes, whose country is International - which is exactly how a neutral athlete is recorded, and a refugee team is the same shape. The check is kept because agreement is overwhelmingly the rule, 303791 participations of 303892 across the two sports that fill the field, so the exceptions are few enough to read one at a time. A sport filling no organization at all has an eligible population of 0 here, which is a sentinel rather than clean data, and GLOBAL-DQ-130 is what reports the absence.

Swimming-DQ-084.reason: a Q that the next round does not honour is either a lost entry or a swimmer who scratched, and nothing found in the database tells the two apart: open question 9 in SPORTS/Swimming.md asks whether a withdrawal is recorded anywhere and is still unanswered. The proportion is therefore the finding - 577 of the sport's heats and 70 of its semi-finals in a population of 11316 - and a single row is a question to ask of that swimmer rather than a defect to repair. unhonoured_competitors names them so the question reaches the right person. Decided 2026-08-26; if a withdrawal is ever found to be recorded, this becomes Actionable and the check becomes a repair list.

Swimming-DQ-073.reason: the sport states an event round in one of two places and never in both, and neither is declared wrong. Round type 329 Heats Summary carries 4095 events and not one says so in its name; 593 say it in the name and leave the round type at 38 or 89, both named with the bare number 1, across 22 templates from 2006 to 2025. The proportion is the finding and no single row is a defect - driving it to zero would mean re-typing 593 events to a convention nobody has declared. It is kept because it measures how far the round vocabulary got, and because the spelling travels with it: the second convention writes Heats Summary, Heat Summary, Heat summary and Slow Heats. Swimming-DQ-072 excludes the bare-number round types outright for this reason and reports only where two meaningful fields contradict. Measured 2026-08-21.

Swimming-DQ-066.reason: the two naming conventions are both live and neither is declared wrong. The proportion is the finding - 92 of 2205 on 2026-08-27, unchanged since 2026-08-20 - and no single row is a defect, so a reviewer driving it to zero would be renaming events to match a convention nobody has declared. Reworded 2026-08-27 after the editions were profiled: it had said the residue marks how far a half-finished cleanup got, and that reading is wrong. Inside an edition the names are uniform and the ids are not - all sixteen relays of the 2025 World Junior Championships are named distance-first while eleven carry the older ids and five the current ones - so the whole disagreement sits on the id side. Which vocabulary an event gets belongs to the competition: the World Championships changed after 2006, the World Junior Championships and the Swimming World Cup never did. The catalogue decision of 2026-08-27 folds 56, 57 and 58 into 365, 367 and 366, and that repair is Swimming-DQ-086's list rather than this one's; this check reaches zero by construction when the fold is done. Decided 2026-08-27

GLOBAL-DQ-089.reason: the sport stores no extra period. SCOPE_TYPE_LIST is 101-105 checkpoint1 to checkpoint5 and 305 final_result, and none of those is an extra-period column; SCOPE_EXTRA_PERIOD_DATA_TYPE_ID has nothing to point at. A swimming race has no continuation to mark with a detailed status. SPORTS/Swimming.md 'Scope types and data types' names the six containers.

GLOBAL-DQ-085.reason: it needs one score stored both as a total on the result row and period by period in the scope layer, where the total is the sum of the periods. Swimming's scope layer holds a cumulative time at a distance, not a summand: the checkpoint values are 4 duration and 296 duration_full_time and adding them together means nothing. The template's own prerequisite excludes a checkpoint split by name, and the sport has no RESULT_FINAL_SCORE_TYPE_ID for it to compare against.

GLOBAL-DQ-086.reason: it reads a per-period score against an approved vocabulary of numbers and sentinels for a period that was not played. Swimming stores no per-period score - scope_result carries 1 rank, 3 comment, 4 duration and 296 duration_full_time, which are the event-level result types repeated at a distance marker - so SCOPE_PERIOD_DATA_TYPE_LIST has nothing to name and there is no not-played sentinel to confirm. The value shapes those columns do carry are audited at event level by Swimming-DQ-039 and Swimming-DQ-047.

GLOBAL-DQ-091.reason: it asserts that every participant of an event stores every period the event contests, reading them from SCOPE_PERIOD_DATA_TYPE_LIST. Swimming's scope layer is checkpoints, not periods: a distance marker with a time, not a segment of the contest that scores. The question the check asks does carry over to a split layer - whether the same checkpoint is recorded for every swimmer in the race - but the structure it reads to ask it is not the one this sport stores, and a signal is read off the structure. Recorded as considered and rejected on 2026-08-20 rather than left unclassified, because it is the one of the five that is not obviously inapplicable.

GLOBAL-DQ-092.reason: it orders periods by ascending data type id and checks that a not-played sentinel never precedes a scored period. Swimming stores no per-period score and no such sentinel, so SCOPE_PERIOD_DATA_TYPE_LIST and SCOPE_PERIOD_SENTINEL_LIST both have nothing to name. Its checkpoint ids do ascend with the race, but there is no sentinel whose position could be wrong.

GLOBAL-DQ-083.reason: head-to-head only per DATABASE.md DB-SEM-015, where an event is a contest between exactly two entries. Swimming is Listing: measured 2026-08-20 its field runs from 1 to 133 participants and averages 10.36, so 44806 of its 45188 events hold more than two and the check would report the sport. SPORTS/Swimming.md records the model and the measurement behind it.

GLOBAL-DQ-119.reason: the sport runs a B final for the swimmers placed ninth to sixteenth in the heats, and that event legitimately ranks its field 9 to 16. This template's start-at-one branch reports every one of them: measured 2026-08-20 it returns 281 events and 191 of those are correct B finals, 68 per cent of its output. Swimming-DQ-046 asserts the same sequence rule with that one branch exempted for a B final and returns the real breaks instead. Semi Final B is not exempt there, because parallel semi-finals each rank from one.

GLOBAL-DQ-076.reason: the template needs a result type carrying a measured quantity that is not a time. This sport has one numeric result type, 100 Rank, and it counts in whole units, so GLOBAL-DQ-124 asserts it on tighter terms. 101 Duration and 557 Full-time duration are clock-notated and the template's own applicability requires them to be left out, which leaves nothing to name.

GLOBAL-DQ-082.reason: it asks whether an event's discipline agrees with its stage's, and requires a stage that groups a single discipline. A swimming stage is a whole championship programme: one stage holds every stroke and distance the meet contests, so the check would report the sport's entire population. GLOBAL-DQ-109 asks the answerable version of the question here, comparing the two places the discipline is stored on the same event.

GLOBAL-DQ-084.reason: head-to-head only. The sport is Listing per DATABASE.md DB-SEM-015 and stores no deciding score at all, so there is no pair of scores that could be tied.

GLOBAL-DQ-087.reason: the sport writes no Winner event property. The field is resolved by result type 100 Rank instead, and the template cannot be instantiated until a Winner exists to read.

GLOBAL-DQ-088.reason: head-to-head only, and it needs both a Winner property and a single deciding numeric score. Swimming stores neither.

GLOBAL-DQ-090.reason: it needs one figure stored in two result types so the pair is a duplicate by design. The sport's five result types are Rank, Duration, Comment, Medal and Full-time duration, and no two of them hold the same figure.

GLOBAL-DQ-093.reason: head-to-head only, for a sport deciding bronze in its own match. Swimming awards its whole medal set inside the one Final, which is what GLOBAL-DQ-037 asserts and this sport instantiates instead.

GLOBAL-DQ-094.reason: head-to-head only, and it reads the place from a pair of scores. There is no deciding score here and the place is already carried by 100 Rank.

GLOBAL-DQ-096.reason: head-to-head only by the competition model, as the template states as a rule. A Listing sport names its events after the discipline and distance, so there are no participants in the name to look for; the sport's own event names are 100m Freestyle and Freestyle 4 x 100m.

GLOBAL-DQ-108.reason: it tightens GLOBAL-DQ-076 on a deciding score that counts scoring units. The sport stores no score of any kind.

GLOBAL-DQ-114.reason: it needs a deciding score and a mirror of it. Swimming stores neither, so there is no pair for one half to be missing from.

GLOBAL-DQ-116.reason: superseded by GLOBAL-DQ-021 and not to be instantiated by any sport, as the template records. GLOBAL-DQ-021 now asks the same question over RESULT_TIE_VALUE_TYPE_LIST, which this sport declares as 557 and 101.

GLOBAL-DQ-117.reason: a sport instantiates this or GLOBAL-DQ-052, never both. This one settles the placing from a stored scalar score and Swimming settles it from a time, so GLOBAL-DQ-052 is the one that can run here and is the stronger test of the two on a timed sport.

GLOBAL-DQ-107.reason: it asserts a scope container on every finished event, and this sport stores splits only for distance and open-water swims. The template takes one SCOPE_TYPE_ID and cannot be told which disciplines are expected to carry one, so instantiating it would report 45477 events that are behaving exactly as the sport intends. SPORTS/Swimming.md records the layer as real but marginal.

GLOBAL-DQ-074.reason: the sport attaches no venue to any event or stage, so all 46379 events are reported and the finding is that fact rather than a list to work through. venue_object is the only mechanism DATABASE.md recognises for it, and Swimming fills none of it. Numbered deliberately on 2026-08-20 with the row count known: the alternative was to declare it not applicable, which would have switched the check off for the day venues start being written.

_names.SPORT_ID: 19 Speed Skating, enet code sp. Short Track Speed Skating is a different sport, sport.id 15, and nothing recorded here was measured against it
_names.CLIENT_FROM_SEASON: 2004, the same client boundary every documented sport carries by the decision of 2026-08-20. The season is read from tournament.name, and this sport's tournament names carry it in both forms the rule covers - a bare year, 2016, and a split season, 2009/2010, which is dated by its last year
_names.OUT_OF_SCOPE_TEMPLATE_ID_LIST: 56 of the sport's 101 templates, by the user's decision of 2026-08-31, which replaces the 2026-08-22 reading that the client took this sport whole. The client names 15 competitions and takes each of them in all three genders, which is why 15 competitions are 45 templates: Winter Olympics, Four Continents Championships, World Championship Single Distances, World Championship Allround, World Championship Sprint, World Allround Junior Championships, World Cup, Junior World Cup, European Championship Allround, European Championship Sprint, European Championship Single Distances, Asian Winter Games, Asian Single Distance Championships, Asian World Allround Championships Qualifier and Youth Olympic Games. The 56 excluded fall in three groups. 26 are the (IOC) mirrors 12731 through 12756, and every one of them mirrors a competition the client keeps - not a single IOC template belongs to a competition that was dropped; they hold 316 tournaments, no stage and no event, and 2301 Comp.Rank statistics. 23 are national championships - Canada, Germany, Netherlands, NM (Norway), North American and USA - and they are the only real loss on the event layer, 465 events and 6989 event participants, all of it Norwegian. The remaining 7 are 25 European Championship mixed, the three World Championship templates 10081, 12339 and 12340, the two World Junior Championships templates 10754 and 12341, and 10947 World Single Distance Junior Championships. Measured 2026-08-31: the boundary takes 5049 of the sport's 9593 Comp.Rank statistics out of scope and leaves 4544, a larger share than it takes of the event layer, because a national championship here carries statistics without carrying events

The shortfall is not a scattered omission and is not what Speed-Skating-DQ-005 asks about: it tracks the statistic's naming generation, the long '<stage> <distance> <gender> - Competition Rank' form carrying the config row and the short '1000 m Male After Run 1' form mostly not. Whether the row is absent is a MISSING_VALUES question that has not been opened; this parameter only names the type so DQ-005 can ask whether a present one is stored twice
_names.ELIMINATION_ROUND_NAME_LIST: semi finals, quarter finals, qualifier, heats and preliminary - the round names after which entries go out, by decision of 2026-08-22. Read by Speed-Skating-DQ-001 and -010. The sport stores all eight of its round types with knockout = 'no', and seven of the eight names also exist under a knockout = 'yes' id, so the judgement decides how many of those pairs are reported: these five are, and they carry 325 events onto the wrong member of their pair. The event names corroborate the round type - 249 of the 325 are named 'Mass Start Semifinal 1' or '2' - so none of the count is the sport behaving normally, which is what the 200-row gate was read for that day

'bronze' sits here and not among the elimination rounds even though H2H sports store its counterpart 138 as knockout = 'yes': in this sport it is a race for third place that ends the competition rather than a match somebody loses their way out of. 'after run 1' is an intermediate standing, not a round with a cut. Putting a name in neither list leaves it unjudged, so the two lists together are the whole judgement Speed-Skating-DQ-001 and -010 rest on

DB-SEM-011 records that it holds a comma-separated list rather than one id. _names.INTEGER_RESULT_TYPE_LIST: the same four, and for a different reason: each counts in whole units by definition. A missed shot, a spare round, a start number and a place are countable things. _names.DUPLICATE_KEY_USES_CALENDAR_DAY: 1. _names.RESULT_COMMENT_VALUE_LIST: the sixty canonical status codes, chosen 2026-08-27 over the ninety-seven spellings actually present. DSQ and Disq. are the same status as Disqualified written three ways, and three spellings of one code is what the check exists to name
_names.RESULT_COMMENT_NO_RESULT_LIST: the three spellings meaning the competitor produced no classified result. DSQ and Disq. were in this list until 2026-08-27 and TOOLS/Test-Package.ps1 refused the combination, correctly: a value absent from RESULT_COMMENT_VALUE_LIST and present here would be reported invalid and honoured as a no-result marker by the same check. Both spellings are still reported, as unrecognised values rather than as contradictions, and the only row that changes reading is one DSQ carrying a full time. LAP and LPD are absent for the opposite reason - a lapped biathlete is stopped on the course and has no time, but does have a place, so listing them would make GLOBAL-DQ-052 report 1504 correct rows as a status contradicting its own rank
_names.STALE_NOT_STARTED_DAYS: 2, the uniform value every sport carries by the decision of 2026-08-06. The rows worth reading are the remainder - 147 DNS holding a place, 16 DNF, and 19 competitors in one Individual carrying no comment at all - and a Monitor keeps them visible without asking anybody to drive 327 events to zero. GLOBAL-DQ-127.reason: the template asserts that competitors holding the same deciding value must share a place, and in the points formats they must not: an Omnium separates riders on equal points by their finish in the last race, so equal points at different ranks is the rule rather than a defect. Measured 2026-08-26, 2148 of 15768 events report and the points races are the bulk of them - one Omnium alone carries 15 tied groups over 50 competitors. Dropping 102 Points from RESULT_TIE_VALUE_TYPE_LIST would cut it to 238, and was rejected the same day: a shared place in a points race does have to agree on points, so the list describes the sport correctly and it is this template that reads the agreement the other way round. Kept because the timed formats, where equal times really must share a place, are audited by the same statement

Track-Cycling-DQ-082.reason: EVENT_TIMED_SPREAD_TOO_WIDE_FOR_ONE_RACE reports that a card does not read like a single race, which is a symptom and not yet a defect: a spread past 1.6 can be a time in the wrong unit, a gap stored without its plus, a rider carried over from another discipline, or a genuine field mixing a world-class rider with a novice at a small meeting. The threshold sits in a measured gap - of 1704 timed events holding three times or more, 1499 spread by less than 1.15 and another 176 reach 1.30, then 17 reach 1.60 - and it returns 12 events of 3053. Its far end overlaps Track-Cycling-DQ-079, which reports what could not have been ridden at all; this one is for what is possible and still does not belong. Recorded 2026-08-26.

GLOBAL-DQ-122.reason: the template asks whether a ranked competitor holds a value in the field the placing is derived from, and in most of this sport the placing is not derived from a stored value at all: a sprint or keirin heat is settled by who crosses first, and the riders carry a rank and nothing else. Measured 2026-08-26, 13209 of 19241 events report - 3468 where no ranked competitor holds a value and 9741 where part of the field does - so the count cannot reach zero while the sport keeps that model. Narrowing RESULT_TIE_VALUE_TYPE_LIST does not help and makes it worse: with 101 alone the count rises to 16258. Kept rather than dropped because the events that do decide on a stored value are the majority of the sport by result volume, and a field missing there is a real defect

GLOBAL-DQ-093.reason: the template reads a final as a two-sided match that awards gold and silver, with bronze decided elsewhere, and this sport runs both conventions at once: a points race final is one race with the whole field and awards all three medals, while a sprint final is two riders and the small final decides bronze. Measured 2026-08-26, 2195 of its 2444 findings are FINAL_UNEXPECTED_BRONZE and every one of them is the sport behaving normally, so the count cannot reach zero however much is repaired. Setting BRONZE_ROUND_TYPE_LIST to 0 does not help - that parameter drives only the separate bronze branch. Kept rather than dropped because the other four branches are sound and account for 249 rows: 224 finals holding places and no medal at all, 19 bronze rounds with none, 4 finals missing gold or silver, and 2 with a medal duplicated

_names.SERIES_SKIP_YEARS: 2020 and 2021, both. With both years named GLOBAL-DQ-081 falls from 16 findings to 7, and those seven are the real ones - the World Cup ending in 2017 where Nations Cup takes over, a World Championships edition missing at 2016, and the South East Asian Games the sport does not always contest

_names.RESULT_SCORE_TYPE_ID: 102 Points, the scalar a placing is read from where the sport does not decide on the clock. The timed formats decide on 101 Duration instead, which is why RESULT_TIE_VALUE_TYPE_LIST names both and this single field cannot
_names.ELIMINATION_ROUND_NAME_LIST: the rounds some riders go out of and the rest go on from. Read the way Speed Skating reads it, 2026-08-26: a final eliminates nobody and belongs in the group list, and so do the placement finals, the small final and the bronze round. The numeric round names 1 through 6 are in neither list, which the parameter contract allows: what they denote is an open question in SPORTS/Track-Cycling.md and a name the sport cannot classify from its name alone is left unjudged rather than guessed
_names.RESULT_COMMENT_VALUE_LIST: every value the Comment result carries, closed at 116 on 2026-08-26 and recorded lower case because GLOBAL-DQ-052 and -117 compare LOWER(TRIM(value)). The vocabulary is a grammar rather than a flat set - a progression phrase naming the round a rider came from, a qualification bracket, a status code, a record marker, and compounds of those joined by a slash - so a new round or a new combination will appear as a finding and is meant to: that is the check working, and the value is added deliberately rather than silently. Never a comma as the separator; the sport combines with a slash
_names.RESULT_COMMENT_NO_RESULT_LIST: the 19 values that mean the competitor holds no classified result: the six plain codes and the thirteen compounds ending in one of them, such as From Final 1-6/DNF. DNQ, REL, Relegated, OVL and LAP are deliberately absent - a rider who failed to qualify, was relegated or was lapped raced and holds a place, so a rank or a time beside them is not a contradiction. GLOBAL-DQ-143.reason: Sentinel, recorded 2026-08-30, and the empty population is itself a defect nobody is reporting. Handball holds 65 Comp.Rank rankings named `(Athletes)`, every one of them paired with its team ranking and every one inside the 39-template client boundary - so the pairing this check needs is there. What is not there is a place. Measured 2026-08-30, those 65 rankings carry 20768 participants and **not one of them carries a `1270 Rank` row**; the only data type they hold is `1429`, the team an athlete belongs to. The 393 team rankings beside them carry `1270` on all 5088 of their participants. Handball is alone in this. Of the six documented sports whose Comp.Rank lists squad members, every other one writes the place on almost all of them: Curling 17122 of 17163, Modern Pentathlon 13377 of 13377, Artistic Gymnastics 13990 of 14069, Speed Skating 12498 of 13241, Triathlon 4525 of 5575. So this is not how the sport stores its rankings, it is what its feed has not sent, and the population is expected to fill rather than never to arrive - which is what makes this a sentinel and not `Not applicable`. **No check in the package reports the gap itself.** It was found while classifying this zero on 2026-08-30 and is recorded in `SPORTS/Handball.md` rather than turned into a check, because Comp.Rank work is paused and a new CheckID needs its own approval.
